## Project overview

This project explores associations between HEXACO personality traits and
teamwork quality using questionnaire data.

It includes an analysis of observed questionnaire data and a Shiny app for
exploring observed relationships and comparing hypothetical team-formation
strategies. Simulated outcomes reflect model assumptions; they are not proven
effects or predictions for real teams.

## Data and scoring

The observed dataset contains questionnaire responses from 54 participants.
The raw file is stored at `data/HEXACO_TWQ_raw-data.csv`. The analysis code
scores HEXACO and teamwork-quality dimensions from the questionnaire items.
The reverse-scoring decisions should be checked against the original study
documentation before interpreting the scores.

## Statistical analysis

The analysis below examines the association between agreeableness and reported
communication quality. The script loads the raw data from the `data/` folder,
creates the scores, fits the exploratory linear model, and prints its summary.

```{r analysis}
source("data_processing.R")
print(communication_plot)
```

The model is exploratory and does not account for participants belonging to
the same team. The sample is small, and the variables were selected after
examining correlations. Interpret the results accordingly; observed
associations do not establish causation.

## Simulation

The simulation generates hypothetical HEXACO profiles and teamwork-quality
outcomes under different team-formation strategies. Its parameters are
assumptions for exploration, not estimates of causal effects.

The standalone `data_simulation.R` script uses the shared
`simulation_core.R` file in the project root. Generated files are written to
`simulated_data/`.

Run this chunk manually when you want to generate new simulation output. It is
not run when knitting this report.

```{r generate-simulated-data, eval=FALSE}
source("data_simulation.R")
```

### Simulation sanity checks

The project includes quick, deterministic checks for the shared simulation
logic. They verify that Random, Balanced, and Similar assignments give every
team the requested number of members, that Balanced and Similar have the
expected between-team variance on a fixed example, and that setting the
composition and diversity effects to zero removes strategy differences when
the same residual draws are used.

Run the checks from the project root, or run this chunk when knitting the
report:

```{r simulation-sanity-checks}
source("sanity_checks.R")
```

The variance ordering is checked on a fixed example so the check is
reproducible; a randomly generated simulation can occasionally show a
different ordering by chance.

## Interactive app

The Shiny app provides controls for exploring observed questionnaire data
and comparing simulated team-formation strategies. From the project root,
launch it with:

```{r launch-app, eval=FALSE}
shiny::runApp("Shiny_App.R")
```

The app and standalone simulation use `simulation_core.R` for shared
simulation calculations. `data_simulation_copy.R` is a separate copy; the
main simulation script documented here is `data_simulation.R`.

## Project files

- `data/` — raw and processed questionnaire data files.
- `figures/` — analysis figures.
- `src/` — additional analysis and modeling scripts.
- `data_processing.R` — scores the observed questionnaire data and fits the exploratory model.
- `data_simulation.R` — standalone simulation script.
- `simulation_core.R` — shared simulation functions.
- `sanity_checks.R` — quick checks for team assignment and strategy outcomes.
- `Shiny_App.R` — interactive Shiny app.
- `main.Rmd` — this report.

## Limitations

The observed sample is small, and participants belong to existing teams.
Analyses should account for that grouping where appropriate. Observed
associations do not establish causation. Simulated results depend on the
assumptions and settings selected in the simulation.

## References

- Zähl, P. (2023). *The Influence of HEXACO Personality Traits on the Teamwork Quality in Student Software Teams — Supplementary Material*. [OSF project](https://osf.io/jb94w/overview); [original dataset download](https://osf.io/download/k4syv/).
